pr_title: Fix Failing Casing Tests with Invariant Culture
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/39522
The test was failing because of a regression on Windows side.
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @tarekgh, @safern, @krwq
Notify danmosemsft if you want to be subscribed.

> Were you able to follow up with Windows?

Yes. I even spent some time debugging it in Windows side as they somehow couldn't easily repro it. Possibly because of some more customization of the version they are using. Windows team still doing more investigation on that.

Reminder: we sometimes have ancient versions of ICU floating around, and it can cause unexpected test failures if we exercise scripts that were introduced within the past few years. See https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/1514#issuecomment-617551026 for some context.

> Reminder: we sometimes have ancient versions of ICU floating around, and it can cause unexpected test failures if we exercise scripts that were introduced within the past few years. See #1514 (comment) for some context.

Yes, we still support ICU version down to v50. but let's see if we run into such issue with this test and then we can fix it.
The CI finished successfully but for some reason showing one of the tasks still running.

issue_context.title: `System.Globalization.Nls.Tests.ToUpper/ToLower_netcore` test failures in local environment
issue_context.body:
### Description

Run tests in `System.Globalization.Nls.Tests` test project. The characters after the ToLower/ToUpper call do not change even though we expect it to change.
```
Test	Duration	Traits	Error Message
System.Globalization.Tests.TextInfoMiscTests.ToLower_Netcore Failed	24 ms		Assert.Equal() Failure            ↓ (pos 1) Expected: 𐐨 Actual:   𐐀            ↑ (pos 1)
System.Globalization.Tests.TextInfoMiscTests.ToUpper_netcore Failed	< 1 ms		Assert.Equal() Failure            ↓ (pos 1) Expected: 𐐀 Actual:   𐐨            ↑ (pos 1)

```

Please note that this only seems to happen when no culture name is specified (`new CultureInfo("")`); the exact same test but with the culture name `en-US` / `fr` / `fr-FR` passes fine.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f4e9146d1d2ba7cf48ab59022658619fc9dbaec3/src/libraries/System.Globalization/tests/System/Globalization/TextInfoTests.cs#L174-L184

### Configuration

* Windows 10 Pro Insider Preview, Build 20170 (Also noticed in a couple previous flights), x64
* Locale ko-KR
* Ran with VS2019 16.7 P4, with `./build.cmd -vs System.Globalization -runtimeConfiguration Release -librariesConfiguration Debug`

### Other information

Possibly a Windows NLS issue, rather than the libraries implementation being wrong? Using builds from the dev channel probably doesn't help a lot 😅

@Gnbrkm41 I am running on Windows 10 v19577 and I am not seeing this behavior. So this most likely a new change coming from Windows. I am trying to confirm that now. Thanks for reporting that.
`System.Text.Tests.RuneTests.Casing_Invariant` under `System.Runtime.Nls.Tests` appears to be failing with the same test data.
do you see any other failures than with this data "\U00010400"?
No, case conversion between `\U00010400` and  `\U00010428` are the only failures I'm noticing with existing test data.

@tarekgh Do you know if Windows ever _removes_ case conversion mappings between versions? Win7 didn't support case conversion between characters from the Deseret alphabet, Win8 did, and now it looks like recent versions of Win10 may have backed it out?

I get the following output with the code:
```
Microsoft Windows 10.0.20170
.NET 5.0.0-preview.8.20361.2
UseNls: True
Invariant: False
\ud801, \udc28,
```

However, I did miss out something when writing the initial issue, that this only seems to happen for the test case when nothing is specified for the culture name (I figured that copying the rows from the test explorer would also copy the details about the data, turns out it doesn't):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42944058/87906456-9e232100-ca9d-11ea-8ffa-6bbe2b18ea48.png)

If I change the value of the string passed into `CultureInfo` to `""`, like this:
```cs
CultureInfo ci = new CultureInfo("");
foreach (char c in ci.TextInfo.ToLower("\U00010400"))
{
    Console.Write($"\\u{(int)c:x4}, ");
}
```
then the code now outputs the following:
```
Microsoft Windows 10.0.20170
.NET 5.0.0-preview.8.20361.2
UseNls: True
Invariant: False
\ud801, \udc00,
```

I will update the top comment to clarify.
Thanks, I'll take a deeper look. this is very helpful.

I discovered this is repro in any WIn 10 machine and not specific to the reported version. Also, the test make sense to fail with the Invariant culture. The question I am trying to find answer for is why this failure didn't show up before?
It is a change in Windows with the Invariant culture. I have reported it to the Windows team. Meanwhile, I'll try to submit a fix from our side to have us immuned against such a change.
